note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Every non-null position cites a source. Never infer from party.

GA-senate.statusNote: Nominees set: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) faces Rep. Mike Collins (R), who won the June 16 runoff.

GA-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Kemp term-limited): Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) faces Rick Jackson (R), who won the June 16 runoff.

candidates.name: Jon Ossoff
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2021, seeking a second term. Investigative journalist before politics. 2026 campaign themes include banning congressional stock trading.

health.label: Defends ACA and pre-existing-condition protections; opposes Medicare for All (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Backs enforcement + pathways reform; voted for the Laken Riley Act (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Calls for repealing 'wasteful, anti-competitive special interest subsidies' and cutting duplicate programs (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Supports Paris Agreement, blocked Okefenokee mine; does not support the Green New Deal (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Opposed defunding police; opposes prison for nonviolent drug offenses, backs cannabis legalization (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Post-Dobbs: Court 'stripped American women of autonomy'; backed Roe-upholding judges (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Champions the John Lewis Voting Rights Act (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Mike Collins
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for GA-10 since 2023; built a trucking company from one semi-truck to a fleet of 115. Won the June 2026 Republican runoff.

immigration.label: Finish the wall, reinstate Remain in Mexico, oppose amnesty and birthright citizenship (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'I will never support a tax increase in Congress'; make TCJA permanent (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Deregulate energy production, 'get government out of the way' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: School choice; opposes critical race theory in schools (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Life 'begins at the moment of conception'; opposes taxpayer-funded abortion (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Backs GA Election Integrity Act, voter ID; opposed H.R. 1 (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Keisha Lance Bottoms
candidates.background: Mayor of Atlanta 2018–2022; later a senior adviser in the Biden White House. Won the May 2026 Democratic primary.

cost.label: Targeted tax relief (teachers, veterans); curb corporate-landlord costs (Branch.vote platform)

health.label: Expand Medicaid to cover more Georgians and save rural hospitals (Branch.vote platform)

housing.label: Address corporate-landlord acquisitions squeezing homeowners and renters (Branch.vote platform)

immigration.label: As mayor: barred city jail from holding ICE detainees; 'welcoming city' (Wikipedia)

education.label: Fully fund Georgia schools; modernize the funding formula (Branch.vote platform)

safety.label: Violence-reduction investment, diversion and reentry programs, universal background checks (Branch.vote platform)

democracy.label: Expand early/absentee voting, Election Day holiday, protect election officials (Branch.vote platform)

candidates.now: White House Office of Public Engagement
priorities: Expand access to affordable health care

candidates.name: Rick Jackson
candidates.background: Healthcare staffing executive and first-time candidate; grew up partly in foster care. Won the June 2026 Republican runoff, defeating the Trump-endorsed lieutenant governor.

cost.label: Freeze property taxes immediately; affordability through tax cuts (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'Make Georgia number one in the nation for deporting criminal illegal immigrants' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Halve the state income tax in 4 years, work to eliminate it in 8 (Ballotpedia)

education.label: 'Parental authority in Georgia classrooms'; ban DEI; freeze public-college tuition (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: 'Ban revolving-door justice'; full support for law enforcement (Ballotpedia)
